To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fuzzy SWRL provides a flexible and powerful framework to represent and reason with vague or imprecision knowledge in the context of the Semantic Web, and it is a promising approach for applications that need to handle vague and imprecise information.
We have developed an approach for extending OWL with fuzzy sets and SWRL with fuzzy sets.

we have proposed and implemented a fuzzy extension to the SWRL language and we have demonstrated the feasibility of our approach by developing and evaluating a fuzzy extension of the Jena SWRL rule reasoner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a fuzzy extension of SWRL, which will enable us to capture imprecision and uncertainty in the representation of knowledge, and to use it in reasoning.
the development and evaluation of a fuzzy extension of SWRL, which can be used in the context of fuzzy multimedia content-based analysis and retrieval.
the design of a fuzzy extension to the SWRL language, which is based on fuzzy set theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fuzzy extension of SWRL is a promising approach to deal with the imprecise and vague information.
the fuzzy extensions of SWR are a useful and practical extension to the existing rule language, providing a powerful mechanism for representing vague or imprecisely defined rules.
the proposed extensions to SWRL provide an important tool for representing imprecision in ontologies and rules, and for reasoning about imprecise knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a fuzzy extension for SWRL.
we have proposed an extension of SWRL that allows for the representation of fuzzy knowledge in rules and the reasoning with such rules.

we propose a fuzzy extension of OWL and SWRL; we propose a fuzzy semantics for OWL; we propose a semantics for SWRL; we show how the semantics can be used to derive the truth value of fuzzy SWRL rules; we show how to use the fuzzy SWRL rules to reason with fuzzy OWL facts
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fuzzy extension of SWRL is a useful tool for the development of applications that require the representation of imprecise knowledge, as it allows the user to represent and reason with imprecise knowledge in the form of rules.
we have shown how fuzzy sets can be used to extend SWRL and OWL to deal with imprecise information.
we have demonstrated that fuzzy logic can be used to extend the capabilities of SWRL and OWL.
